title: Every building, rock and bug nest on my RTS map started as an AI image. Here's the whole first mission at 8K detail, zoom in
author: Failosipher
selftext:
This is the bug-infested colony from the first mission of my RTS, Engines of Hate, from the in-game camera angle at 13,803 x 6,598.

Every object in it went through the same pipeline:

* concept art from image gen (GPT, then Gemini to clean it up)
* the concept turned into a 3D model in Meshy
* a low-poly version so I can place hundreds of them without killing the framerate

This map has 115 different models placed 429 times: ruined buildings, cliffs, rock formations, nests, tendrils, roads, wrecks, dead colonists. The whole game is at \~386 Meshy models now. That's hundreds and hundreds of images, and a LOT of hours of generating, picking the good one, fixing what Meshy got wrong and re-doing it. (The only exceptions are the soldiers, which are an Asset Store pack, and the ground, which is Unity terrain.)

The shot itself is Claude Code too. I have a custom MCP bridge into the Unity editor, so Claude read the game camera's angle, rendered 56 orthographic tiles at that angle and stitched them in Python. The fun part: HDRP volumetric fog doesn't render in ortho cameras, so the first version came out half as bright. Claude shot matched perspective/ortho pairs and fit a color curve to put the haze back. The whole thing takes about 25 seconds.

Me: layout, art direction, deciding what's good. Claude writes most of the code.

The playtest is open on Steam if you want to see it in motion: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5375880/Engines\_of\_Hate/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_campaign=r\_aigamedev\_1102](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5375880/Engines_of_Hate/?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=r_aigamedev_1102)

Latest devlog (the new colony buildings and how they break apart): [https://failosipher.itch.io/engines-of-hate/devlog/1745860/lets-see-if-i-regret-this-system-in-a-week](https://failosipher.itch.io/engines-of-hate/devlog/1745860/lets-see-if-i-regret-this-system-in-a-week)

Happy to go deeper on any step, lmk
